QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r18.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r18.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r18.claim: Although they admit God created them when asked, they revert to error and persist in it.
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r18.anchor: ولئن سألتهم عن خالقهم لأقروا ، ولكن إذا عادوا إلى غيهم نقضوا وأصروا

RAZI-FULL:v18p178#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p178#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p178#3/r1.claim: Many acknowledged God as creator yet assigned worship to others; the verse’s believers are thus polytheists in worship despite recognizing God.
RAZI-FULL:v18p178#3/r1.anchor: أنهم كانوا مقرين بوجود الإله بدليل قوله : { ولئن سألتهم من خلق * السماوات والارض ليقولن الله

RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r1.claim: After citing creation of the heavens and visible and hidden favors, al-Razi says the polytheists still admit God made them; since all creation needs Him, all praise belongs to Him and none besides Him should be worshipped, though they do not understand.
RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r1.anchor: لما استدل بخلق السموات بغير عمد وبنعمه الظاهرة والباطنة

RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r2.claim: The verse also consoles the Prophet: their return will soon reveal his truth and their falsehood, even before the Resurrection, because their admission that God created heaven and earth supports monotheism and exposes their association.
RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r2.anchor: لا تحزن على تكذيبهم فإن صدقك وكذبهم يتبين عن قريب

RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r3.claim: The command to praise God responds to the public vindication of the Prophet’s truth and the deniers’ falsehood.

RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r4.claim: One analysis leaves the verb know wholly without an object, as in saying someone gives and withholds; another supplies the understood object that all praise belongs to God.
RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r4.anchor: استعمالا للفعل مع القطع عن المفعول بالكلية

RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r5.claim: Al-Razi says the absolute construction, denying them any knowledge at all, is more emphatic than saying they do not know that all praise belongs to God.
RAZI-FULL:v25p136/r5.anchor: والثاني أبلغ لأن قول القائل : فلان لا علم له بكذا

STUDYQURAN:31:25/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:25/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:25/r1.claim: The Quraysh idolaters acknowledged God as creator because a supreme creator was evident to them and many still believed in a supreme deity.
STUDYQURAN:31:25/r1.anchor: the idolaters among the Quraysh—would surely say, “God” (cf. 10:31

STUDYQURAN:31:25/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:25/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:31:25/r2.claim: Praise for the created order belongs to God alone, not to beings that did not create it.
STUDYQURAN:31:25/r2.anchor: only God should be praised for the existence of the created order, not those who had nothing to do with bringing forth creation (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:31:25/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:25/r3.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:31:25/r3.claim: The command to praise God means that no being other than God should be worshipped.
STUDYQURAN:31:25/r3.anchor: no being other than God should be worshipped (Z)

BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r1.claim: Even idolaters admit God created the celestial and terrestrial bodies because the fact is too evident to deny.
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r1.anchor: الأجرام العلوية والسفلية {ليقولن} خلقهن {الله} لغاية وضوح الأمر بحيث اضطروا إلى الاعتراف به

BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r2.claim: Praise follows because God made the signs of oneness so clear that even obstinate deniers scarcely reject them.
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r2.anchor: على أن جعل دلائل التوحيد بحيث لا يكاد ينكرها المكابرون أيضا

BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r3.claim: Most fail to act on their admission by abandoning shirk and worshipping God alone.
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r3.anchor: {بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون} شيئا من الأشياء فلذلك لا يعملون بمقتضى اعترافهم بأن يتركوا الشرك

BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r9.claim: Entrusting, relying on God, sincerity, turning from all else, tawḥīd, and obedience lead to Paradise and nearness; disbelief, shirk, showing off, and reputation-seeking lead to fire and separation.
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r9.anchor: منها أن التفويض والتوكل وإخلاص القصد والإعراض عما سوى الله والإقبال على الله بالتوحيد والطاعة من موجبات حسن العاقبة

BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r10.speaker: الشيخ العطار
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r10.claim: ʿAṭṭār's couplet says worldly success is useful at the end only if one has sincerity; otherwise the soul is lost.
BURSEVI:v7p69#4/r10.anchor:
قال الشيخ العطار قدس سره :
زر وسيم وقبول كار وبارت نيايد دردم آخر بكارت

TAB-FULL:v18p571/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p571/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p571/r1.claim: When asked, the polytheists acknowledge that God created heaven and earth; Muhammad is to praise God, who creates, unlike their powerless idols.
TAB-FULL:v18p571/r1.anchor: الحمد لله الذي خلق ذلك، لا لمن لا يخلق شيئا وهم يخلقون

TAB-FULL:v18p571/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p571/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p571/r2.claim: Most of the polytheists do not know who truly deserves praise or where gratitude is due.
TAB-FULL:v18p571/r2.anchor: بل أكثر هؤلاء المشركون لا يعلمون من الذي له الحمد، وأين موضع الشكر

TABATABAI:31:22-25/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:22-25/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:22-25/r5.claim: Polytheists are disposed toward monotheism: asked who created heaven and earth, they acknowledge God without recognizing the implications.
TABATABAI:31:22-25/r5.anchor: إشارة إلى أنهم مفطورون على التوحيد معترفون به من حيث لا يشعرون

TABATABAI:31:22-25/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:22-25/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:22-25/r6.claim: Since governance cannot be separated from creation, acknowledging God as Creator entails that he governs, gives and withholds, and alone is the hoped-for and feared deity.
TABATABAI:31:22-25/r6.anchor: وإذا كان الخالق هو هو فالمدبر لها هو هو لأن التدبير لا ينفك عن الخلق

TABATABAI:31:22-25/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:22-25/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:22-25/r7.claim: The Prophet is told to praise God for the polytheists' unwitting admission; most fail to understand that it entails God's exclusive lordship and divinity.
TABATABAI:31:22-25/r7.anchor: أمره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يحمد الله على اعترافهم من حيث لا يشعرون

TABATABAI:31:22-25/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:22-25/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:22-25/r8.claim: A few understand the implication but refuse the truth and deny what they inwardly know, as in the account of Pharaoh's people.
TABATABAI:31:22-25/r8.anchor: نعم قليل منهم يعلمون ذلك ولكنهم لا يطاوعون الحق بل يجحدونه وقد أيقنوا به

TABRISI:31:21-25/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:21-25/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:21-25/r17.claim: When asked who created the heavens and earth, they answer that it was God.
TABRISI:31:21-25/r17.anchor: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن

TABRISI:31:21-25/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:21-25/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:21-25/r18.claim: Muhammad, or any listener, is told to praise and thank God for guidance and the enabling grace of knowing Him.
TABRISI:31:21-25/r18.anchor: على هدايته لنا وتوفيقه إيانا لمعرفته

TABRISI:31:21-25/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:21-25/r19.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:31:21-25/r19.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi explains this as thanking God for a religion whose truth even one's opponent must acknowledge because its proof is clear.
TABRISI:31:21-25/r19.anchor: وقيل: معناه اشكر الله على دين يقر لك خصمك بصحته لوضوح دلالته عن الجبائي

TABRISI:31:21-25/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:21-25/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:21-25/r20.claim: Most people do not understand the proof that stands against them.
TABRISI:31:21-25/r20.anchor: لا يعلمون } ما عليهم من الحجة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:24-25/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:24-25/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:24-25/r3.claim: If asked who created the heavens and earth, they acknowledge that it was God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:24-25/r3.anchor: ولئن سالتهم من خلق السموات والأرض ليقولن الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:24-25/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:24-25/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:24-25/r4.claim: Praise God, who created the heavens and earth.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:24-25/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:24-25/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:24-25/r5.claim: They show their ignorance by associating partners with God after acknowledging that He created the heavens and earth.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:24-25/r5.anchor: إذ أشركوا به بعد إقرارهم بأنه خالقهما

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679/r8.claim: When asked who created the heavens and earth, they answer God; most do not know that they will be resurrected.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p679/r8.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {ولئن سألتهم من خلق السموات والأرض ليقولن الله قل الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون} [لقمان: 25] أنهم مبعوثون.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r1.claim: The idolatrous Arabs believed in God and acknowledged his creative power when asked, but worshipped and sought refuge in idols as intermediary gods, falling into shirk.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r1.anchor: Putperest Araplar, aslında Allah’ın varlığına inanıyor, sorulduğunda O’nun yaratıcı kudretini tanıdıklarını ifade ediyorlardı; fakat putlarını aracı tanrılar saydıkları için Allah’ı bırakıp putlara tapıyor

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r2.claim: Saying all praise belongs to God means no other being may receive divinity, divine function or sanctity, or be worshipped.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r2.anchor: Allah’tan başka hiçbir varlığa tanrılık sıfatı, işlevi ve kutsallığı yüklenemeyeceği, ibadet edilemeyeceği anlamını içermektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r3.claim: The passage from verse 26 to the sūra’s end answers why all praise belongs exclusively to God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r3.anchor: 26. âyetten sûrenin sonuna kadar devam eden kısım, neden bütün övgülerin Allah’a mahsus olduğu sorusunun âdeta cevabı mahiyetindedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r7.claim: The exclusive-praise claim rests on three premises: God’s absolute freedom to govern, knowledge beyond human comprehension, and power to create, sustain, or end all things with ease.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:25/r7.anchor: 25. âyetteki “Bütün övgüler Allah’a mahsustur” hükmü, 27-29. âyetlerde şu üç öncüle dayandırılmıştır

BURHAN:v3p133/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p133/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p133/r4.claim: The answer omits خلقهن because the preceding question already supplies it: “God created them.”
BURHAN:v3p133/r4.anchor: والتقدير خلقهن الله فحذف خلقهن لقرينة تقدمت في السؤال

DAMGHANI:v1p47/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p47/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p47/r2.claim: Faith can refer to professing God while remaining in shirk; the People of the Book also accept some scripture while rejecting other parts and the messengers.
DAMGHANI:v1p47/r2.anchor: الرابع : الإيمان في شرك . كقوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

ASAD-NOTES:31:25#n23/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:31:25#n23/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:31:25#n23/r1.claim: People give the answer that God created everything from vague habit, without seeing that acknowledging Him as ultimate cause logically requires surrender to Him alone.
ASAD-NOTES:31:25#n23/r1.anchor: a cognition of God as the Ultimate Cause of all existence logically postulates one's full surrender to Him, and to Him alone

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r6.speaker: opponents
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r6.claim: When asked who created the heavens and earth, even the opponents acknowledge that God did.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r6.anchor: they will answer that it is God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r7.claim: Since they acknowledge God as creator of everything, Islahi says He alone deserves gratitude.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r7.anchor: if they acknowledge God to be the creator of everything, then He alone is worthy of gratitude.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r8.claim: It is illogical to credit others who had no role in creating or governing the universe.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r8.anchor: others who neither have any role in creating this universe nor governing it?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r9.claim: The statement that most do not know means their practice is unreasoned: they miss the consequences of premises they accept and deny in practice what they acknowledge.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p121/r9.anchor: The words َونُمَلْعَی َلَا ْمُهُرَثْكَأُ ْلَب imply that what they do is not based on any reasoning.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r10.claim: Their answer establishes that they acknowledge God as creator of the entire world while still invoking another deity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r10.anchor: ليقولن الله: أقام الحجة عليهم بأنهم يقرون بأن الله هو خالق العالم بأسره، ويدعون مع ذلك إلها غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r11.claim: Praise is due to God for making the proof against them manifest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r11.anchor: قل الحمد لله على ظهور الحجة عليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r12.claim: The phrase elides a clause: their claim is not valid, since no informed person would affirm a deity besides God; most fail to know this.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p418#2/r12.anchor: بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون: إضراب عن مقدر، تقديره: ليس دعواهم، نحو: لا يعلمون أن ما ارتكبوه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r1.claim: Asked who created the heavens and earth, the polytheists answer Allah; the author prefers the implied wording 'Allah created them' over 'Allah is their creator.' Their admission is forced by obviousness.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r1.anchor: أي خلقهن الله تعالى وجوز أن يكون التقدير الله خلقهن والأول أولى

ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r2.claim: Praise God for compelling their admission, which entails that only the true creator and benefactor deserves worship and invalidates associating others with Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r2.anchor: على إلزامهم وإلجائهم إلى الإعتراف بما يوجب بطلان ما هم عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, praise is for making the signs of monotheism so clear that even an obstinate disputant cannot deny them.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r3.anchor: وجوز جعل المحمود عليه جعل دلائل التوحيد بحيث لا ينكرها المكابر أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r4.claim: Most do not know that their admission obligates the conclusion; the ending elegantly extends the thought to their ignorance of why God is praised here.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r4.anchor: أن ذلك يلزمهم قيل : وفيه إيغال حسن

ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r5.claim: The author refers readers to his fuller discussion of the parallel in al-Ankabut 29:61.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p96#3/r5.anchor: تمام الكلام في نظير الآية في العنكبوت فتذكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p291/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p291/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p291/r7.claim: They acknowledge that God created the heavens and earth, yet most do not know what that acknowledgment entails.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p291/r7.anchor: ليقولن الله قل الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r3.claim: The proof that no one besides God can create is so clear that the idolaters are compelled to admit He created the heavens and earth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r3.anchor: لوضوح الدليل المانع من إسناد الخلق إلى غيره بحيث اضطروا إلى إذاعته

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r4.claim: The command to praise God follows because their forced admission proves their own belief false.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r4.anchor: على إلزامهم والجائهم إلى الإعتراف بما يوجب بطلان معتقدهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:24-27/r5.claim: Most fail to understand what their admission logically entails.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p27/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p27/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p27/r4.claim: The disbelievers argue while admitting that God created heaven and earth, an admission that entails His exclusive creative lordship and should compel submission to His unity.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p27/r4.anchor: ولما كان من أعجب العجب مجادلتهم مع إقرارهم بما يلزمهم به قطعا التسليم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p27/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p27/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p27/r5.claim: For this surah's wisdom-oriented purpose it suffices to state the subject, الله; al-Zukhruf, whose aim is fuller exposition, uses a fuller formulation.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p27/r5.anchor: لم يزد هنا على المسند إليه بخلاف الزخرف التي مبناها الإبانة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p27/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p27/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p27/r6.claim: Their confession shows that everything they associate with God is itself one of His created artifacts, not a partner in creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p27/r6.anchor: فقد أقروا بأن كل ما أشركوا به بعض خلقه ومصنوع من مصنوعاته

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r1.speaker: امرأة ذي النور الدرسي
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r1.claim: A woman associated with Dhu al-Nur al-Dawsi asks whether children should be feared from the idol Dhu al-Shara, illustrating belief that idols could act.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r1.anchor: قالت امرأة ذي النور الدرسي رضي الله عنه : هل يخشى على الصبية من ذي الشرى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r2.speaker: قوم ضمام بن ثعلبة
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r2.claim: When Dammam ibn Thaʿlaba's people heard him revile their gods, they warned him to beware leprosy and vitiligo, showing their fear of idols' power.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r2.anchor: وكما قال قوم ضمام بن ثعلبة رضي الله عنه لما سبب آلهتهم : اتق الجدام اتق البرص

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r3.speaker: ثقيف
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r3.claim: The custodian of al-ʿUwwa and Thaqif feared divine retaliation when their cult objects were attacked; after Thaqif said the foundations would rage, al-Mughira ibn Shuʿba excavated them.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r3.anchor: قالت ثقيف في طاغيتهم , حتى أنهم قالوا عندما سويت بالأرض , والله ليغضبن الأساس

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r4.claim: When afflicted, especially at sea, the idolaters disavow their idols and attribute events to God, as exclusive divine control requires.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r4.anchor: إذا مستهم الضراء لا سيما في البحر تبرؤوا منها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r5.claim: One reading is that most know God is the sole controller but fail to act on that knowledge; knowledge without practice is effectively no knowledge and may be worse than ignorance.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r5.anchor: إن الله هو المنفرد بكل شيء كما أنه تفرد بخلق السماوات والأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r6.claim: Alternatively, they have no useful knowledge at all, since any knowledge of God would benefit them.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r6.anchor: أو يكون المعنى أنه لا علم لهم أصلا إذ لو كان لهم علم لنفعهم في علمهم بالله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r7.claim: Another reading is that they do not affirm God's exclusive creation and provision, a contradiction that obliges them to accept the Prophet's claim of absolute divine unity.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p29/r7.anchor: فيكون ذلك موجبا لتناقضهم وملزما لهم بالإقرار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r1.claim: The verse follows the condemnation of ancestral imitation in 31:21: they inherit polytheism yet acknowledge that God created heaven and earth, exposing their irrational inconsistency.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة { وإذا قيل لهم اتبعوا ما أنزل الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r2.claim: Heaven and earth encompass their contents, including the stones from which idols are made.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r2.anchor: ما يشمل ما فيها من المخلوقات ومن بين ذلك حجارة الأصنام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r3.claim: This surah’s لا يعلمون varies stylistically from al-‘Ankabūt’s لا يعقلون while conveying the same meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p179/r3.anchor: تفننا في المخالفة بين القصتين مع اتحاد المعنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r14.claim: Idolaters admit God created the world yet worship others; “praise God” means praise Him for making the proof clear.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r14.anchor: بأنهم يقرون بأن الله تعالى خالق المخلوقات ويدعون مع ذلك إلها غيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r15.claim: “Rather, most of them” shifts from an omitted proposition such as “their claim is false.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r15.anchor: بل أكثرهم إضراب عن مقدر تقديره ليس دعواهم بحق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r16.claim: “Most” is literal because Zayd ibn ʿAmr, Quss, and Waraqa ibn Nawfal were exceptions; it may also refer to those destined to convert.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p353#2/r16.anchor: منهم من شذ فعلهم كزيد بن عمرو بن نفيل، وقس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348/r1.claim: The polytheists acknowledge God alone created the heavens and earth, yet worship partners they admit are His creation and property; their confession establishes proof, though most do not understand.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p348/r1.anchor: إنهم يعرفون أن الله خالق السموات والأرض، وحده لا شريك له، ومع هذا يعبدون معه شركاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r1.claim: The command to praise God binds them to the implication of their confession that He alone created the heavens and earth, deserves thanks, and alone should be worshipped.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r1.anchor: إلزام لهم على إقرارهم بأن الذي خلق السماوات والأرض هو الله وحده ، وأنه يجب أن يكون له الحمد والشكر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r2.claim: Most people fail to understand that the confession obliges them to this conclusion and do not heed it when reminded.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p507#2/r2.anchor: أن ذلك يلزمهم ، وإذا نبهوا عليه لم ينتبهوا

MUQATIL:31:25-26/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:25-26/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:25-26/r1.claim: Asked who created the heavens and earth, the unbelievers answer God; most nonetheless do not know His oneness.
MUQATIL:31:25-26/r1.anchor: بتوحيد الله عز وجل، ثم عظم نفسه عز وجل، فقال:

NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#5/r1.claim: Their admission that God alone created the heavens and earth entails that praise and thanks belong to Him alone and that no one else should be worshipped with Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#5/r1.anchor: الزام لهم على اقرارهم بأن الذى خلق السموات والأرض هو الله وحده وأنه يجب ان يكون له الحمد والشكر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#5/r2.claim: Most do not understand that this admission binds them to worship God alone, and fail to notice when reminded.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p285#5/r2.anchor: أن ذلك يلزمهم واذا نبهوا عليه لم يتنبهوا

QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r1.claim: Since they admit God created the heavens and earth, the author asks why they worship someone else.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله } أي هم يعترفون بأن الله خالقهن فلم يعبدون غيره.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r2.claim: Praise belongs to God for guiding people to His religion; no one else deserves it.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r2.anchor: { قل الحمد لله } أي على ما هدانا له من دينه، وليس الحمد لغيره.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r3.claim: Most of them do not know because they neither consider nor reflect.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:25-26/r3.anchor: { بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون } أي لا ينظرون ولا يتدبرون.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p100/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p100/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p100/r2.claim: The opponents’ own confession that God created heaven and earth entails that He alone deserves worship and gratitude; He is self-sufficient, sovereign, and needs no intercessor to win His favour.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p100/r2.anchor: They confess that the heavens and the earth are created by God. So the question is that when He is the creator, how can someone else be worthy of worship and gratitude?
